**Hub path:** `server/router/api/v1/sse_hub.go` (endpoint handler in `server/router/api/v1/sse_handler.go`, event constructors in `server/router/api/v1/sse_event_helpers.go`)
**Handlers that broadcast:** `CreateMemo`, `UpdateMemo`, `DeleteMemo`, `CreateMemoComment`, `SetMemoAttachments`, `SetMemoRelations`, `UpsertMemoReaction`, `DeleteMemoReaction`

The hub is `SSEHub` in `sse_hub.go`, with `Subscribe`, `Unsubscribe`, `Broadcast`, and `Close`, plus a per-client `canReceive` filter so private memos only reach permitted users. Event types are enumerated there:

```15:20:server/router/api/v1/sse_hub.go
	SSEEventMemoCreated        SSEEventType = "memo.created"

	SSEEventReactionUpserted   SSEEventType = "reaction.upserted"
	SSEEventReactionDeleted    SSEEventType = "reaction.deleted"
```

The route is registered by `RegisterSSERoutes` (line 25 of `sse_handler.go`), which is wired into the Echo group in `server/router/api/v1/v1.go` (line 125).

- `CreateMemo` — `server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go:163` (suppressed when called internally from `CreateMemoComment`)

**`APIV1Service.DispatchMemoCreatedWebhook` — `server/router/api/v1/memo_service_webhooks.go`; `internal/webhook`; HMAC-SHA256 per the Standard Webhooks spec**

`APIV1Service.CreateMemo` calls the dispatcher at `server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go:157`. The dispatcher (line 15 of `memo_service_webhooks.go`) delegates to the shared `dispatchMemoRelatedWebhook` with activity type `memos.memo.created`, which resolves the memo creator, loads that user's webhooks via `Store.GetUserWebhooks`, and hands each one to `webhook.PostAsync` (line 71) — so delivery is asynchronous and non-blocking.

The HTTP delivery lives in `internal/webhook/webhook.go`: `PostAsync` enqueues onto a bounded queue and `Post` (line 120) performs the actual `POST` of the JSON payload through a `safeClient`, checking the status code and the response body's `code` field.

Signing, when the hook has a secret, is done in `Post`:

```142:149:internal/webhook/webhook.go
		mac := hmac.New(sha256.New, key)
		mac.Write([]byte(msgID + "." + timestamp + "."))
		mac.Write(body)
		signature := base64.StdEncoding.EncodeToString(mac.Sum(nil))

		req.Header.Set("webhook-id", msgID)
		req.Header.Set("webhook-timestamp", timestamp)
		req.Header.Set("webhook-signature", "v1,"+signature)
```

The signed content is `msgID + "." + timestamp + "." + body`, the result is base64-encoded and sent as `webhook-signature: v1,<sig>` alongside `webhook-id` and `webhook-timestamp`. Secrets use the `whsec_<base64>` form generated by `GenerateSigningSecret` (line 111) and decoded by `resolveSigningKey`; validation of user-supplied secrets is in `internal/webhook/validate.go`.

**Engine: CEL (Common Expression Language, via `github.com/google/cel-go`) — `internal/filter/`, entry point `internal/filter/engine.go`**

**Mechanism:** the filter string is compiled by a CEL environment into an AST, lowered into a dialect-independent condition tree (intermediate representation), and then rendered into a parameterized SQL `WHERE` fragment by a dialect-aware renderer that each driver invokes with its own `DialectName`.

How the pieces fit together:

- `Engine.Compile` builds a CEL AST (`cel.NewEnv` at line 25, `cel.AstToParsedExpr` at line 57 of `internal/filter/engine.go`); the allowed fields and functions come from `internal/filter/schema.go`, with `DefaultEngine()` supplying the memo schema.
- `internal/filter/parser.go` and `internal/filter/ir.go` convert the parsed expression into a `Condition` tree.
- `internal/filter/render.go` turns that tree into SQL, branching per dialect. For example, date-part extraction differs three ways:

```231:239:internal/filter/render.go
	case DialectSQLite:
		base = fmt.Sprintf("CAST(strftime('%s', %s, 'unixepoch') AS INTEGER)", spec.sqlite, col)
		off = spec.off[0]
	case DialectPostgres:
		base = fmt.Sprintf("CAST(EXTRACT(%s FROM to_timestamp(%s) AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AS INTEGER)", spec.pg, col)
		off = spec.off[1]
	case DialectMySQL:
		base = fmt.Sprintf("%s(%s)", spec.mysql, col)
```

Placeholder style and string-length functions (`LENGTH` vs `CHAR_LENGTH`, line 297) are handled the same way.

- Drivers call the shared helper `filter.AppendConditions` (`internal/filter/helpers.go:9`), which compiles each filter with `CompileToStatement` and appends the resulting SQL and bound args to the query's `where`/`args` slices. The call sites are `store/db/sqlite/memo.go:57–61` (with `filter.DialectSQLite`), `store/db/postgres/memo.go:54`, and `store/db/mysql/memo.go:65`.

The filter reaches this path from `APIV1Service.ListMemos` in `server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go`, which puts the expression into `store.FindMemo.Filters`. The same CEL machinery backs saved shortcuts (`Shortcut.filter` in `proto/api/v1/shortcut_service.proto`) and user filtering in `server/router/api/v1/user_service_filter.go`; supported syntax is documented in `internal/filter/README.md`.

**Interceptor: `web/src/connect.ts` (with token storage in `web/src/auth-state.ts`); tokens: short-lived JWT access token in memory/`Authorization: Bearer`, refresh token in an HTTP-only cookie, and Personal Access Tokens for programmatic clients; backend: `server/auth/`**

On the frontend, `authInterceptor` (line 156 of `web/src/connect.ts`) is attached to the shared Connect transport (line 188) and does three things: it attaches the access token as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`, it proactively refreshes when the token is near expiry (`getRequestToken`, lines 124–150), and on a `Code.Unauthenticated` response it refreshes once, replays the request with an `X-Retry` marker, and redirects to login if that fails.

The refresh token is never touched by JavaScript — it rides along as a cookie because the transport uses `fetch` with `credentials: "include"` (line 57–62), and refresh calls go through a separate `refreshTransport` with no interceptors to avoid recursion (line 65). Concurrent refreshes are deduplicated by `tokenRefreshManager` (line 30), which matters because server-side refresh tokens rotate.

On the backend, validation lives in `server/auth/` — `Authenticator` in `server/auth/authenticator.go` exposes `AuthenticateByAccessTokenV2` (JWT signed with the server secret), `AuthenticateByRefreshToken` (parsed, then checked against the stored token row via `GetUserRefreshTokenByID`), and `AuthenticateByPAT` (hash lookup through `GetUserByPATHash`, with expiry and last-used tracking). `AuthenticateToUser` tries the `Authorization` header first and falls back to the refresh cookie. Token minting/parsing is in `server/auth/token.go`, header/cookie extraction in `server/auth/extract.go`, and context plumbing in `server/auth/context.go`.

This authenticator is invoked from both protocol paths: the gateway middleware in `server/router/api/v1/v1.go` and the Connect interceptor chain, with per-RPC public/anonymous exceptions listed in `server/router/api/v1/acl_config.go`.
